title: JRE 2258 - Steven Rinella
guestBio: Steven Rinella is an outdoorsman, conservationist, writer, and host of "MeatEater." Look for his new audio original "MeatEater's American History: The Mountain Men (1806-1840)" on February 11, 2025. His new show "Hunting History With Steven Rinella" on HISTORY begins on January 28.
tldr: Steven Rinella discusses his new HISTORY channel show 'Hunting History With Steven Rinella' premiering January 28, 2025
Audio original 'MeatEater's American History: The Mountain Men (1806-1840)' launches February 11, 2025
Conversation covers the history and culture of American mountain men and frontier hunting traditions
Rinella shares insights from decades of hunting, conservation work, and outdoor expertise
Discussion explores how historical hunting practices shaped American expansion and settlement
Focus on MeatEater's evolution as a media brand and educational platform for outdoor enthusiasts
recap:
Joe welcomes Steven Rinella to JRE 2258, diving deep into the outdoorsman's latest projects and his passion for hunting history. Rinella is riding high with multiple launches coming in early 2025, including his new HISTORY channel show 'Hunting History With Steven Rinella' starting January 28 and an audio original called 'MeatEater's American History: The Mountain Men (1806-1840)' dropping February 11. These projects represent Rinella's evolution from hunting show host to serious historian and documentarian.

The conversation touches on Rinella's deep knowledge of American frontier history and how hunting culture was intrinsically tied to exploration and settlement. He breaks down the methodology behind creating educational content that respects both the historical record and the skill sets of the hunters who shaped the nation. Rinella talks about how MeatEater has grown from a niche hunting show into a comprehensive media brand that educates people about conservation, hunting ethics, and outdoor skills.

Throughout the episode, Rinella shares his perspective on why these historical narratives matter today, especially in the context of modern conservation efforts and the disconnect many Americans have from their food sources. The discussion flows naturally between personal hunting stories, historical facts, and broader commentary on how outdoor traditions are being preserved and passed down. Rinella comes across as genuinely knowledgeable about his subject matter while remaining accessible and engaging, which is clearly part of MeatEater's success.
